title: Runbook: match-engine Kafka consumer lag
subtitle: Diagnose, drain, and escalate lag on cg-match-engine-prod-v2 (clh.settlement.inbound.v2)
author: Aman Kumar
audience: On-call engineer (cold), Diego Alvarez (SRE), Kavya Menon (match-engine), Helen Cho (ops), Priya Nair (escalation)
owners: Aman Kumar (runbook), Diego Alvarez (Burrow / Kafka), Kavya Menon (match-engine code)
related: CLH-TDD-2023-008 (ingest redesign), CLH-TDD-2022-021, CLH-5519, CLH-RB-2024-007 (worker OOM, later), PagerDuty: clh-recon-lag
summary: On-call runbook for Kafka consumer lag on match-engine, consumer group cg-match-engine-prod-v2, topic clh.settlement.inbound.v2 (72 partitions). Page if aggregate lag is above 400,000 for 10 minutes on a peak settlement day (16:00-21:00 ET). This is written so someone cold can tell lag from a stuck partition, scale replicas vs poison payload, use kafka-consumer-groups.sh and Burrow, and run Helm without guessing. If you only read one section, read 3 (decide) then 5 (commands).
form_description: Operational runbook for Clearhaven match-engine consumer lag. Written for the primary on-call to execute without the author on the call.
revision_history: First draft after April 4 staging drain (2.1M lag).
Diego review. Page policy 400k / 10 min. Helm caps.
Helen added cash-desk comms. Priya approved page policy.
Approved. Added poison vs scale decision table and cold-start checklist.

blocks.text: 0. Cold start (do this first)

You are on-call for clh-recon. PagerDuty service clh-recon-lag fired, or Helen Cho pinged #clh-ops that breaks are late. You do not need the full TDD. You need to know whether matching is slow, stuck, or poisoned, and whether cash desk should treat the 7pm ET window as degraded.

items: Join #clh-ops and #clh-recon-oncall. Say you have the page. Do not debug silently for 20 minutes.
Open Burrow: http://burrow.clh.prod.northstar.internal/v3/kafka/clh-kafka-prod/consumer/cg-match-engine-prod-v2/status (also Grafana dashboard Clh Match Lag, uid clh-match-lag).

If it is 16:00-21:00 ET US settlement day, treat this as peak. Off-peak, the same lag number is still real but the page threshold is 400k/10 min only for peak; off-peak we page at 400k/25 min. Check the clock.
Do not restart match-engine as step 1. Restart rebalances 72 partitions and adds lag. Do not rewind offsets. Do not delete the consumer group.

If Helen asks 'are we short?': lag is a processing delay, not a cash position. Say that. If breaks are not opening because unmatched is also delayed, tell her the window signal may be late. Marcus Bell pages cash desk only after Helen asks, not because lag is red.

blocks.label: Do not
blocks.text: Do not kafka-consumer-groups.sh --reset-offsets on cg-match-engine-prod-v2 unless Priya and Diego both say so. A reset duplicates matches or drops them. Do not helm rollback match-engine because lag is high; rollback is for bad code, not for a broker blip. Do not raise maxReplicas above 36.
1. Preconditions

This runbook assumes the CLH-5519 cut has happened: live topic is clh.settlement.inbound.v2, 72 partitions, group cg-match-engine-prod-v2, namespace clh-recon-prod, cluster eks-clh-prod-use1. If you still see cg-match-engine-prod (no -v2) and inbound.v1, you are on the old path. Stop and read CLH-TDD-2023-008. Mixing commands across v1/v2 is how you reset the wrong group.

You need: kubectl context clh-prod-use1, network to clh-kafka-01.prod.us-east-1.northstar.internal:9092 (or exec into kafka-tools-0 in namespace clh-kafka-prod), Helm 3, and Okta group clh-oncall-prod. If kubectl get ns clh-recon-prod fails, you are on the wrong context. Fix that before any helm command.

blocks.caption: Access and where to run commands
rows: git, not ad-hoc set of random flags

blocks.text: Kafka brokers: clh-kafka-01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06 .prod.us-east-1.northstar.internal. Schema registry clh-schemareg-01.prod.us-east-1.northstar.internal:8081. Postgres recon-match-01.prod.us-east-1.northstar.internal. If you cannot reach brokers from your laptop, exec into kafka-tools-0. All of this stays in us-east-1. Do not jump to a west-region tools box.
2. Page policy

Page (PagerDuty clh-recon-lag -> primary): aggregate lag > 400,000 for 10 consecutive minutes during 16:00-21:00 ET on a US settlement day. Peak days can be 8.2 million records; 400k is about 5% of a peak day sitting in the pipe, which at 740 rec/s on a hot partition is still many minutes if it is stuck rather than draining. Off-peak (nights, weekends, US holidays Helen posts in #clh-ops): 400k for 25 minutes, or 1.2M for 10 minutes any time.

Warning (Slack #clh-recon-oncall, no page): lag > 80,000 for 3 minutes (this is also the HPA input). DLQ depth on clh.settlement.inbound.v2.dlq > 50. Replica lag on recon-match-01 > 15s (that is a different runbook-ish path; it will look like match lag because commits stall).

Do not page on a single partition lag of 50k if aggregate is 60k and the partition offset is still moving. That is a hot key (account 4418-CLEAR is the usual one). Watch it. Page if that partition's CURRENT-OFFSET is unchanged for 3 minutes while LAG > 10,000. Unchanged offset is stuck. High lag with moving offset is behind.

blocks.caption: Lag vs stuck vs poison (interpret this before you scale)
rows: DB wait or GC, not lack of pods
do not scale past 36; watch, section 6.3

blocks.text: 3. Decision (skim if you are drowning)

blocks.label: Decision tree
blocks.text: Moving offset + high CPU: scale to min(current*2, 36) and wait 8 minutes. Moving offset + low CPU: do not scale; check Postgres commit p95 and GC. Offset frozen on one partition: poison path, do not scale. Lag jump after a Kafka change window: drain, cap 36, no second broker roll. If you have not identified which row you are in within 6 minutes, call Diego. Guessing Helm is slower than a 2 minute SRE voice call.

Rejected 'fix' we already burned: lag-only HPA to 40+ pods. Staging April 4 exhausted IPs at 38. maxReplicas is 36 in values.prod.yaml. If you --set autoscaling.maxReplicas=48 you will get a second incident. The April 4 drain of 2.1 million lag took 19.4 minutes at 34 pods. That is the envelope. You will not beat it by adding 12 more pods on a cluster that cannot schedule them.
4. What healthy looks like

Quiet afternoon: aggregate lag 0-12,000, 18 pods, commit p95 8-12ms, hottest partition under 400 rec/s. Peak burst (CDC + RailClear catch-up): lag 20,000-80,000 for a few minutes, HPA to 24-30, hottest partition around 740 rec/s, e2e still inside 8.8 min on an 8.2M shape if nothing else is wrong. After 21:00 ET lag should fall under 5,000 unless a late file landed. A late file is Helen's world; ask her before you chase 8,000 lag at 21:40.

Burrow status OK means every partition's lag is inside Burrow's thresholds, which we set to 15,000 per partition warning. Burrow STOP means a partition is not consuming. STOP is closer to stuck than to 'a bit behind.' Grafana panel 'parts in STOP' should be 0. If Burrow is down, use kafka-consumer-groups.sh. Do not page just because Burrow 500s; check the CLI.
5. Commands (engineer execute)
5.1 Context and group describe

blocks.caption: Always describe before you change anything
blocks.text:
kubectl config use-context clh-prod-use1
kubectl -n clh-recon-prod get deploy match-engine -o wide
kubectl -n clh-recon-prod get hpa match-engine

kubectl -n clh-kafka-prod exec -it kafka-tools-0 -- bash
export BROKERS=clh-kafka-01.prod.us-east-1.northstar.internal:9092
export GRP=cg-match-engine-prod-v2

kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server $BROKERS --group $GRP --describe

# sum lag and max partition lag (column 6 is LAG on our image; confirm header first)
kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server $BROKERS --group $GRP --describe | head -1
kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server $BROKERS --group $GRP --describe \
  | awk 'NR>1 && $6 ~ /^[0-9]+$/ {s+=$6; if($6>m){m=$6;p=$3}} END {print "sum_lag=" s, "max_lag=" m, "max_part=" p}'

Confirm the header. On the kafka-tools image we pin (confluentinc/cp-kafka:7.3.1), columns are GROUP TOPIC PARTITION CURRENT-OFFSET LOG-END-OFFSET LAG CONSUMER-ID HOST CLIENT-ID. If someone upgraded the image, LAG may not be $6. Look at the header. If CURRENT-OFFSET is '-' the member is not assigned. That is a rebalance in progress or a group with no members. Check pod count.
5.2 Stuck vs behind (watch offsets)

blocks.caption: Sample the same partition twice, 90 seconds apart
blocks.text:
# pick the max_part from above, example partition 17
PART=17
kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server $BROKERS --group $GRP --describe \
  | awk -v p=$PART '$3==p {print}'
sleep 90
kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server $BROKERS --group $GRP --describe \
  | awk -v p=$PART '$3==p {print}'

# if CURRENT-OFFSET identical and LAG > 10000: stuck -> section 8
# if CURRENT-OFFSET increased: behind -> section 6 or 7
5.3 Burrow

blocks.caption: Burrow status and per-partition (from laptop on VPN)
blocks.text:
curl -sS http://burrow.clh.prod.northstar.internal/v3/kafka/clh-kafka-prod/consumer/cg-match-engine-prod-v2/status | jq .
curl -sS http://burrow.clh.prod.northstar.internal/v3/kafka/clh-kafka-prod/consumer/cg-match-engine-prod-v2/lag | jq '.status.partitions[] | select(.current_lag > 10000)'

# Grafana: dashboard uid clh-match-lag, variables cluster=clh-kafka-prod, group=cg-match-engine-prod-v2
# Panels: aggregate lag, p95 handle ms, commit p95, pods, parts STOP, DLQ offsets

Burrow complete=true and status=OK is healthy. ERR or STOP on a partition: note the partition id, go to 5.2. If Burrow says the whole group is ERR and CLI shows members, Burrow may be stale; trust CLI for 5 minutes, ping Diego to restart Burrow only if both disagree for 10 minutes. Restarting Burrow does not drain Kafka lag. It drains your confusion.
5.4 App and DB signals

blocks.caption: Pods, logs, commit latency, DLQ
blocks.text:
kubectl -n clh-recon-prod get pods -l app=match-engine -o wide
kubectl -n clh-recon-prod top pods -l app=match-engine
kubectl -n clh-recon-prod logs deploy/match-engine --tail=100 --all-containers=true | grep -E 'poison|SQLTransient|pause|rebalance'

# metrics (svc scrape)
kubectl -n clh-recon-prod port-forward deploy/match-engine 18080:8080
# other terminal:
curl -sS localhost:18080/actuator/prometheus | grep -E 'match_db_commit|kafka_consumer_lag|jvm_gc_pause'

# DLQ high watermark
kubectl -n clh-kafka-prod exec -it kafka-tools-0 -- \
  kafka-run-class.sh kafka.tools.GetOffsetShell --broker-list $BROKERS \
  --topic clh.settlement.inbound.v2.dlq --time -1

commit p95 over 80ms is the circuit that shrinks poll size to 40. Lag will rise while that is on. That is intended. Killing pods to 'reset' the circuit makes it worse. If top shows one pod at 2 CPU and others at 0.1, assignment may have collapsed after a bad rebalance; section 6.2.
6. Scale replicas (only if the table said so)

HPA should already be trying. Check it before you helm. If current replicas is 18 and CPU is 70% and lag is 500k moving, HPA may be waiting. You can patch minReplicas up for the evening. You cannot patch max above 36.

blocks.caption: Helm / HPA scale. Cap is 36.
blocks.text:
# look first
kubectl -n clh-recon-prod get hpa match-engine -o yaml | less

# temporary min bump for the window (example 18 -> 28). max stays 36.
helm upgrade --install match-engine charts/clh-match-engine -n clh-recon-prod \
  -f charts/clh-match-engine/values.prod.yaml \
  --reuse-values \
  --set replicaCount=28 \
  --set autoscaling.minReplicas=28 \
  --set autoscaling.maxReplicas=36 \
  --wait --timeout 10m

kubectl -n clh-recon-prod rollout status deploy/match-engine

# after drain, put min back to 18 the same way. Do not leave min=28 overnight.

concurrency per pod is 2. 36 pods * 2 = 72 partitions. More pods than 36 means idle members and longer rebalances. If helm upgrade hangs, ctrl-c does not roll back. Check rollout, then kubectl -n clh-recon-prod rollout undo deploy/match-engine only if the new RS is crashlooping, not if lag is still high.
6.2 Rebalance storm

If describe shows CONSUMER-ID flapping and lag not falling, you have a rebalance loop. Causes we have actually seen: max-poll-interval exceeded (poison or DB stall), session.timeout too low, someone set partition.assignment.strategy back to range. Logs will say MemberId ... leaving. Fix: do not add pods. Find the pod that is not heartbeating (logs, or the one restarting). kubectl -n clh-recon-prod delete pod <that-one> once. If all pods are leaving, check Postgres. A total group collapse with 36 deletes is a worse rebalance. Call Diego.
6.3 Hot key (4418-CLEAR)

Partition lag high, offset moving, one pod CPU high. Scaling does not split a partition. You wait it out or you have a match-engine bug on that key. Check open_key count for that account in Postgres (section 7). If open_key for one account is hundreds of thousands, matching may be failing to close keys. That is Kavya, not Helm.
7. When it is Postgres or GC, not Kafka

blocks.caption: Quick DB checks (read-only)
blocks.text:
psql $RECON_MATCH_URL -c "select now()-pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp() as replica_lag;"
psql $RECON_MATCH_URL -c "select wait_event_type, wait_event, count(*) from pg_stat_activity where datname='recon_match' group by 1,2 order by 3 desc;"
psql $RECON_MATCH_URL -c "select count(*) as open_keys from recon_match.open_key;"
psql $RECON_MATCH_URL -c "select left(account,12) a, count(*) from recon_match.open_key group by 1 order by 2 desc limit 10;"

open_key above 2 million is a matching bug (see CLH-TDD-2022-021). Page Kavya. Replica lag over 15 seconds: recon-query will go unready; match-engine writes to primary so it may still drain, but commits can pile up. Diego owns Postgres. You do not failover RDS because match lag is high unless Diego is on the call and the primary is actually dead.

GC: jvm_gc_pause_seconds p99 over 2s correlates with session timeout. One pod. Delete that pod once. If every pod GC storms, heap is wrong (values set Xmx to 1536m on a 2Gi request). Do not raise heap in the incident above 1536m without Diego; you will OOM and enter the worker-OOM path. Note it for a ticket.
8. Poison payload (stuck partition)

Offset frozen, one partition, usually after a connector glitch. match-engine should DLQ after three failures. If a throwable is classified as retryable forever (SQLTransient mis-tagged, or a NullPointer on a field we thought required), the poll never commits and the partition dies.

items: Identify partition P and the pod assigned (HOST column in describe, map to pod IP).
If you see the same record_id three times then a DLQ line, wait 30s. Offset should move. If it does not, the commit after DLQ failed. Restart that one pod once.

If you see the same record_id 20 times and no DLQ, isPoison() is wrong for this throwable. Temporary: scale that pod's concurrency cannot skip the record. Last resort skip is a skip-record flag MATCH_SKIP_RECORD_IDS we shipped for this, comma-separated, on that deployment only. Set it, wait for offset to move, unset it. File a ticket with the record_id. Do not leave the flag set.

Dump the record for Kavya: kafka-console-consumer with --partition P --offset <CURRENT> --max-messages 1, Avro decoder via schema registry. Save to the ticket, not to Slack (payloads are settlement data, us-east-1, still sensitive).

blocks.caption: Skip flag (last resort) and unset
blocks.text:
# only after steps 1-3, only the stuck record_id
helm upgrade --install match-engine charts/clh-match-engine -n clh-recon-prod \
  -f charts/clh-match-engine/values.prod.yaml --reuse-values \
  --set env.MATCH_SKIP_RECORD_IDS=rc-7f3aa91c \
  --wait --timeout 8m
# watch CURRENT-OFFSET on that partition until it moves, then:
helm upgrade --install match-engine charts/clh-match-engine -n clh-recon-prod \
  -f charts/clh-match-engine/values.prod.yaml --reuse-values \
  --set env.MATCH_SKIP_RECORD_IDS= \
  --wait --timeout 8m

blocks.label: Skip is a control event
blocks.text: Skipping a settlement record means match-engine will not see it unless we replay from DLQ later. Comment on CLH-5519 or open a child ticket. Tell Helen the record_id. Do not skip a batch of ids because you are tired. One id, then unset.
9. Drain after a broker roll or produce flush

If lag jumps by a million in a few minutes and offsets are moving, you are in the April 4 shape. Brokers 01-06, change freeze 16:00-21:00 ET. If someone rolled anyway, you drain: HPA to 36, do not rewind, do not roll another broker, do not restart the consumer group. 19.4 minutes was the staging number for 2.1M. Prod hardware is larger. Still budget 25 minutes before you invent a new plan.
Tell Helen: window signal may be late, not wrong. Tell Marcus only if Helen wants cash desk notified. Cash desk hearing '2 million lag' sounds like $2 million. It is record count. Say records.

items: Confirm ISR on inbound.v2 is 3. If ISR is 1, you have a broker problem, Diego first, stop scaling stories.
Confirm produce is flowing (log-end-offset increasing on several parts).
Watch commit p95. If > 80ms, wait for the circuit. Do not delete pods.
Write times in #clh-ops: jump start, peak lag, drain complete. Numbers.

blocks.text: 10. When it fails (the runbook path failed)

If after 25 minutes of a moving-offset drain lag is still above 400k and CPU is low, you missed a DB lock. Call Diego and Kavya. If after 10 minutes of a frozen offset the skip flag is not moving it, the assigned consumer is not that deployment (wrong group, or a shadow group in prod). Describe GROUP and look at CLIENT-ID. Shadow group cg-match-engine-shadow-v2 should not exist in prod. If it does, that is an incident of its own; scale to 0 the shadow deploy.

If helm upgrade errors on values, you used a local chart that is not tagged. Prod deploys from the Git tag the last successful ship used. Find it in Argo or in #clh-deploys. Do not helm from your laptop's dirty tree.

blocks.caption: Escalation
rows: Lag, moving, CPU high, under 36 pods
Lag, moving, CPU low / commit p95 high
Cash desk thinks we are short
PD escalate, she will pull people

blocks.text: 11. Comms to ops (copy/paste)
Templates. Fill the numbers. Do not paste internal heap dumps to Helen.

blocks.caption: Slack to #clh-ops
blocks.text:
match-engine lag: aggregate= records, max partition=

lag=, offsets . Action: . Window signal: . This is record lag, not a cash position. Next update in 10 min.
If you used MATCH_SKIP_RECORD_IDS, say so in #clh-ops with the id. Helen would rather know a row was skipped than hunt a ghost break at 21:00.

Burrow vs Grafana as source of page? Today both, PD uses Grafana alert.

blocks.text: Q3 is the one that might add process to section 8. Until Leah answers, skip remains last resort with a ticket. Q4 should be yes; I will nag Kavya if the PR is not up by June 30. A shadow consumer in prod steals partitions and looks exactly like stuck lag.

After you close the page: leave minReplicas where you found it (18), paste the describe sums in the PD note, and if you skipped a record, the child ticket number. Runbook owner is still Aman through Q3. Diego owns Burrow uptime. Kavya owns isPoison() misses.
